name: Leon Mehta
life: “I still remember getting a wig back in much better condition than I lent it.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Leon watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I sold her the wig. I want to help her give it away without telling the next owner its history.
appearance: Leon has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Look for a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a narrow-striped sweater with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. In conversation Leon looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Leon admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Leon learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To get the wig to its next wearer on agreed terms.
family: Jay Choi is Leon’s younger cousin. Leon makes the call. Jay is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The missing name on the stern*, Jay says, “I transposed two letters in my first language and put the brush down when I saw the owner seeing it.”
connections: Peyton Ho. Giving away the old wig takes a different decision from keeping an old brush.

reactions.response: Leon lets the client keep or give away the wig without explaining the change of mind.

reactions.response: Leon repeats the correct name quietly, making the correction easy to hear without turning it into a performance.
